title: DEMONSTRATION / behavior test — archaeological and material research

units_of_analysis: Ground-stone tool surfaces and assemblages in early farming settlement contexts; experimental comparative surfaces
phenomena_or_topics: Microwear-based functional inference about plant-processing practices
relationships_or_questions: Which wear attributes and analytical procedures support proposed plant-processing functions?
How are experimental reference collections and alternative worked materials used to test attribution?
How do raw material, surface preservation, reuse and depositional context affect interpretability?
What can tool-level functional inference support about settlement practices, and which steps require independent contextual evidence?
contexts: Early farming settlements defined regionally through source chronology and subsistence context
geographic_scope: No regional restriction proposed; retain region-specific farming chronology rather than assume a universal Neolithic date
scope.temporal_scope: Early farming defined in each regional archaeological context; no publication-year restriction proposed
languages: Proposed initial English screening; other languages flagged for human translation decision
source_types: Original archaeological microwear analyses and relevant experimental reference studies; contextual assemblage and botanical reports where linked

subquestions: Which wear attributes and analytical procedures support proposed plant-processing functions?
How are experimental reference collections and alternative worked materials used to test attribution?
How do raw material, surface preservation, reuse and depositional context affect interpretability?
What can tool-level functional inference support about settlement practices, and which steps require independent contextual evidence?

concept_definitions.definition: Tools shaped or used through grinding, pecking or abrasion, including grinding slabs and handstones; exclude chipped-stone-only assemblages
concept_definitions.label: ground-stone tools

concept_definitions.definition: Microscopic surface observations used for functional interpretation; record resolution, surface preparation and criteria rather than assume all polish is diagnostic
concept_definitions.label: microwear analysis

concept_definitions.definition: Actions such as grinding, pounding or dehusking plant materials; taxa and action specificity require independent warrant
concept_definitions.label: plant-processing practices

concept_definitions.definition: Settlement context with regionally explicit evidence of early cultivation or farming; no universal date boundary
concept_definitions.label: early farming settlement

include: Original microwear investigation of ground-stone tools from contextually identified early farming settlements with traceable methods and functional reasoning
Experimental ground-stone studies testing plant and plausible alternative contact materials, retained as analogical reference rather than settlement evidence
Associated residues or botanical evidence only when their relationship to the analyzed tools or context is explicit
exclude: Chipped-stone-only analyses and macroscopic typology without microscopic functional evidence
Unprovenienced artifacts where settlement linkage cannot be established; classify uncertainty before exclusion
Plant-processing assertions based solely on tool shape, and experiments lacking relevant ground-stone surfaces

databases: Proposed: multidisciplinary index and archaeological report repositories
strategy_groups: Combine ground-stone synonyms with microwear terms; use plant-processing and early-farming variants for targeted searches without requiring those interpretations in every broad query
Plan reference tracing for experimental comparison methods and linked excavation reports, separating analogical references from settlement cases
